name: What happens if hidden damage is found after the pool is drained?

mainEntity.name: What happens if hidden damage is found after the pool is drained?
mainEntity.text: What happens if hidden damage is found after the pool is drained?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden damage is common in pool remodels because many problems only become visible after draining and demolition. Contractors may uncover shell cracks, failed plumbing, hollow coping, rust around fittings, water intrusion, or deck movement. When this happens, the proper response is to pause, document the issue, and explain the repair options before moving forward. Homeowners should expect that some projects will need change orders if the original inspection could not reveal everything. The size of the change depends on whether the damage is isolated or widespread. Small repairs may only add a modest amount of time and cost, while larger structural issues can affect the entire schedule. To reduce risk, ask the contractor how they handle hidden conditions and whether the estimate includes a contingency for discoveries after drain-out. A well-written contract should explain approval steps for added work so there are no surprises. The key is to treat hidden damage as part of a transparent process rather than an excuse for vague pricing.
acceptedAnswer.description: If hidden damage is found after draining, the contractor should stop, document the issue, and provide a revised scope and price before continuing. Common surprises include cracks, hollow coping, failed plumbing, rust, or deck movement. The remodel schedule and budget may change depending on how extensive the damage is.
